QUOTE: With assembly it is `asm volatile("" : "+r"(x))`, so the compiler cannot see through the value. Without assembly it is `x ^ mbedtls_ct_zero`, where `mbedtls_ct_zero` is a `volatile` global defined in `library/constant_time.c`.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says that without assembly the function XORs with the volatile global `mbedtls_ct_zero`, and it names that global. It doesn't say the global holds zero, but the name and the "volatile-zero trick" wording imply it.
